title: 29 Years After Border, Sunny Deol Called Himself 'Dharmendra's Son' — and Nobody Could Speak
excerpt: The Ikka trailer landed with tears, laughter, and Netflix India calling it 'the next Dhurandhar' — streaming worldwide July 10
body:
The trailer opens with **Sunny Deol**'s voice, low and gravelly, and it sounds nothing like the man who once bellowed *dhai kilo ka haath* across a generation of living rooms. He's quieter now. More deliberate. And when the end credits flash "Dharmendra's son, Sunny Deol," you feel every year of that silence.

<youtube></youtube>

**Ikka** dropped its trailer on June 29 from a five-star hotel in Mumbai, and what was supposed to be a slick Netflix launch turned into something rawer — part reunion, part memorial, part masterclass in how two of Bollywood's most private actors operate when the cameras aren't rolling.

Sunny plays Arjun Mehra, a celebrated defense attorney whose moral compass has never wavered — until he agrees to defend **Akshaye Khanna**'s Shauryamann Gaur in a high-profile attempted murder case. The kind where personal loyalties get mangled by legal procedure, and nobody walks out clean.

> "Hum court mein jeetne ke liye nahi, haq ke liye ladte hai." — Arjun Mehra

We don't fight to win. We fight for what's right. Classic Sunny. Except this time, he might be wrong.

The last time these two shared screen space, they were soldiers in J.P. Dutta's **Border** (1997) — a film that defined patriotism for an entire generation of Indians at home and abroad. Twenty-nine years later, they're on opposite sides of a courtroom, and the friction between them looks electric. Akshaye, in particular, appears to be operating at an elevation most actors never reach — cold, manipulative, deeply layered, every frame suggesting a man who knows exactly which strings he's pulling.

Sunny was asked about their reunion during the launch. His answer was quintessentially him — blunt, affectionate, slightly bewildered.

> "Woh mere se bhi zyada aloof hai! But he's a gem of a guy." — Sunny Deol

He then added, with visible warmth: "Tab bahut mazaa aaya tha aur iss film mein bhi bahut mazaa aaya. I met him after so many years." It's worth noting that Akshaye didn't actually attend the launch. His voice note was played at the beginning of the event instead — which, if you know anything about Akshaye Khanna, is the most Akshaye Khanna move possible.

But the moment that truly stopped the room had nothing to do with Akshaye or courtrooms. It was the end-credit title card: "Dharmendra's son, Sunny Deol." **Dharmendra** — Bollywood's original He-Man, the man whose smile could light up a decade — passed away on November 24, 2025, at 89. When a journalist asked Sunny about the tribute, the 68-year-old kept it to five words: "I will always be my father's son." That was all he said. And it was enough.

**Tillotama Shome**, who plays fierce public prosecutor Madhura Banerjee, was the launch event's unexpected star. The actress — known for arthouse gems, not franchise courtroom dramas — delivered anecdote after anecdote that revealed the peculiar social ecosystem of a major Bollywood set.

On meeting Sunny for the first time: "I didn't even want him to say hello to me. I feared ki woh chidd jaayenge." But her director, **Siddharth P. Malhotra**, insisted she talk to him. So she looked into his eyes. "Have you ever seen a cow's eyes?" she asked the room. "They are very kind. And I realized that he has really kind eyes."

On Akshaye: "I have NEVER seen Akshaye Khanna smile! But one day, after pack-up, this man came towards me and smiled. I just smiled and walked off. Then he called my name. And it was Akshaye Khanna. I couldn't recognize him kyunki woh smile kar rahe the!"

Meanwhile, **Dia Mirza** — playing Arjun's wife Avantika — raised her own moment of panic about slapping Akshaye on camera. "Am I going to get into a lot of trouble?" she asked nervously. "He has a phenomenal fan following." Sunny stepped in, heroically: "Why are you so worried? You're playing MY wife!" The room erupted.

Netflix India's head **Monika Shergill** set the stakes plainly: "Ikka will be the Dhurandhar of Netflix." Given that Akshaye's **Dhurandhar** was one of the biggest Hindi OTT hits of the past year, that's not just confidence — it's a declaration.

For the diaspora, this is a Day One watch. Ikka premieres globally on Netflix on **July 10** — no theatrical window, no staggered release, no hunting for regional screenings. San Jose, Toronto, London, Sydney — you press play at the same time as Mumbai. The cast also includes **Sanjeeda Shaikh** and **Akansha Ranjan Kapoor**.

Sunny admitted he'd tried for years to make **Damini 2**, the sequel to his iconic 1993 courtroom drama, but it never materialized. "Then I got Ikka," he said simply. Tillotama's husband told her to stop taking herself so seriously and do mainstream cinema — so she did. And Akshaye Khanna, the man who never smiles, sent a voice note instead of showing up.

The courtroom finally called them all back. July 10 can't come fast enough.
